questions.question: A 10-second recording sampled at 16 kHz contains how many waveform samples?
options: 160,000 frames
16,000 samples
1,600,000 samples
160,000 samples
questions.explanation: A waveform stores one value per sample, so 16,000 samples/second × 10 seconds = 160,000 samples. The 16,000-sample option counts only one second; “160,000 frames” names later analysis windows, not raw waveform values.

questions.question: Using frame_len = 400 and hop = 160, how many complete frames come from 160,000 samples?
options: 998 frames
999 frames
1,000 frames
997 frames
questions.explanation: The code counts one starting frame plus complete hops: 1 + floor((160,000 − 400)/160) = 998 frames. Rounding 997.5 hops up adds a partial final window; 1,000 also ignores the 400-sample frame length.

questions.question: Why take a logarithm of spectrogram magnitudes before feeding common audio models?
options: It changes the waveform sampling rate automatically
It removes every quiet frequency from the signal
It converts frequency bins into time frames
It compresses a very wide range of magnitudes
questions.explanation: Log magnitude compresses the several-orders-of-magnitude range so weak and strong spectral components fit a more manageable scale. The “removes every quiet frequency” option confuses compression with filtering: log scaling changes magnitudes but keeps the frequency bins.

questions.question: With n_fft = 400, how many one-sided DFT bins feed the mel filterbank?
options: 400 frequency bins
80 frequency bins
200 frequency bins
201 frequency bins
questions.explanation: A real-valued FFT keeps n_fft/2 + 1 bins on one side, so 400/2 + 1 = 201, including DC and Nyquist. The 200-bin option omits one endpoint; 80 is the mel-output count, not the FFT input size.

questions.question: Training used 80 mel bins, while inference produces 128. What is the likely diagnosis?
options: The model will ignore the extra bins safely
The waveform must be converted into MFCCs first
The mel scale will automatically merge the bins
A feature-shape mismatch must be resolved
questions.explanation: The model was trained for 80 mel features per frame, so producing 128 changes the input shape and feature contract. The mel scale defines filter spacing; it does not reconcile a model trained on a different number of output bins.

questions.question: A classifier must resolve brief drum hits. Which framing choice best matches the lesson’s trade-off?
options: Use a shorter window and hop for transient detail
Use a longer window and hop for transient detail
Use a longer window and shorter hop for transient detail
Use a shorter window and longer hop for transient detail
questions.explanation: Brief drum attacks need high time resolution, so the lesson favors a short window and a short hop; its transient example is 5 ms/2 ms. The “longer window and shorter hop” choice samples often but still smears a brief attack inside each long frame.
